text: Pi 5 keeps rebooting whenever I plug in my external SSD. Works fine without it.
why: The word 'SSD' triggers the storage rule. A person reads 'reboots when I add a load' and knows it is the power supply.

text: Ordered a Pi 5 last Tuesday and it still hasn't shipped. Can you check?
why: No product keyword at all. Both the rule and a person route it away from technical support.

text: Green light comes on but nothing on the monitor. Tried two HDMI cables.
why: No keyword matches. The rule has no entry for a symptom described without naming a component.

text: Camera module 3 not detected. libcamera-hello says no cameras available.
why: 'camera' appears literally. This is the case keyword rules are good at, and it is why they get written.

text: wifi drops every few minutes on my Pi 4 but ethernet is rock solid
why: 'wifi' matches. Lowercase and unpunctuated, which the rule survives and a stricter one would not.

text: My board died after 3 months. It's still under warranty right? I want a replacement.
SD card corrupted twice this month. Using a SanDisk 64GB. Is this a known issue?
Not a support request — just wanted to say the docs for the camera are excellent.
why: The single most instructive row. 'camera' matches, so the rule files praise as a camera fault. A keyword rule cannot tell you the sentence is not a complaint.

text: Won't boot from USB after the firmware update. Was working before. Pi 4, 8GB.
why: 'boot' appears literally, and here it happens to be right.

text: Under heavy compile the board throttles and then the USB devices disconnect. Official 27W supply.
why: Right answer, wrong reasoning, and the accuracy number cannot tell you. The rule matched 'supply' inside 'Official 27W supply' — the clause where the customer is ruling the power supply OUT. It files this correctly by accident. Week 6 is where a judge can finally see the difference between right and right-for-a-reason.
